item.title: Author Event with Peter Jaros — Sun Sep 13, 3:00 PM — Pocket Books Shop
item.description:
Join Franklin & Marshall professor Dr. Peter Jaros as he celebrates the publication of his new book The Corporate Forms of Antebellum U.S. Literature in conversation with his colleague Dr. Erik Anderson. Haven’t brushed up on your early 19th-century literature in a while? Don’t worry: no prior knowledge or reading required for this event.
You’ll get to learn about how in the early 19th century, the corporate form was still a wobbly category that writers used as a vehicle for imagining both personhood and politics in strange and surprising ways. And you’ll have the chance to talk about why anyone in 2026 would want to read books from the early 1800s & what exciting intersections there might be between law and literature.
Register Now
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.description: Tuesdays in September 15, 22 & 29 | 5:30 – 6:45 PM Led by Sarah Shelton, Urban Well Yoga Studio Coordinator, and The Reverend Stacey Carpenter, Associate Rector at Saint James The Practice of Recovery: Yoga, the 12 Steps and a Path for All is a three-week series exploring recovery, healing, and embodied practice in everyday life. item.title: Evening Compline — Tue Sep 15, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: PDF@Zoetropolis Presents Everything Everywhere All At Once — Thu Sep 17, 6:30 PM — Zoetropolis Cinema Stillhouse
item.description:
What if you could see every life you might have lived? Would you find yourself—or lose yourself among the possibilities? The Zoetropolis America 250 series continues its exploration of Reinvention & Transformation with Everything Everywhere All at Once.
Michelle Yeoh stars as Evelyn Wang, a Chinese American immigrant juggling a struggling laundromat, an IRS audit, and a family she can’t quite hold together—until an encounter with the multiverse sends her hurtling through the lives she might have led. Wildly inventive, funny, and moving, the film takes America’s promise of self-reinvention to an extraordinary extreme. If we could become anyone, what would make this particular life worth choosing? And can kindness offer a meaningful response to a world that seems increasingly overwhelming?

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
